title: Multiplexed session replayer with per-tenant p95 gating and regression alerts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Build a high-fidelity, tenant-aware load harness that replays multiplexed streaming chat/completion sessions over SSE and WebSocket while measuring tokens/sec and per-tenant p95 latency, and automatically detecting regressions. The harness should emulate realistic user behavior (think-time, message size distribution, token bursts, KV-cache warm/cold cycles), support per-tenant quotas and routing policies, and feed structured telemetry into our observability pipeline for regression gating and alerting.

Scope and constraints:
- Generate sustainable sustained token rates (10k-200k tokens/sec aggregate) with configurable multiplexing (sessions per connection).
- Support both SSE and WebSocket protocols, including connection-level multiplexing and simulated network jitter.
- KV-cache awareness: run cold-start and warmed-cache scenarios to surface p95 differences.
- Per-tenant metrics: p95, p50, tokens/sec, error-rate, connection churn.
- Regression detection: EWMA + percentile drift detection over rolling windows, automatic alert to PagerDuty via Alertmanager if tenant p95 regresses >20% sustained for 5m.
- Reproducibility: deterministic seeds for synthetic prompts and tokenization where possible.
- Lightweight worker-based architecture so we can scale across k8s pods without GPU dependency (clients only), but able to drive Dedicated clusters and Redwood Hosted endpoints.

Design notes:
- Driver architecture: central coordinator (stateless) + workers that open N multiplexed connections; each worker simulates M tenants and S sessions/tenant. Coordinator assigns scenarios (cold/warm/jitter/burst) and collects telemetry via gRPC reporting endpoint.
- Protocol layer: pluggable adapters for SSE and WSS; adapters expose same session lifecycle hooks (open, send-chunk, receive-chunk, close).
- Tokenization and prompt templates: templates modeled from production prompt corpus (anonymized), lengths follow a log-normal distribution; content generation uses small deterministic lexicon to avoid PII.
- Telemetry: send structured events to observability with labels {tenant, region, protocol, cache_state, session_id}. Metrics emitted: tokens_generated, tokens_per_sec, p95_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, downstream_error_count, conn_open_time_ms. Traces should include session-level spans for open/send/kv-lookup/receive.
- Regression logic: maintain rolling baseline from last N hours (configurable). Compute relative drift for p95; use EWMA to smooth spikes. Regression gate trips when relative_drift >= threshold && sustained_duration >= window.

Acceptance criteria (must be all met):
- Harness can run 8h sustained without coordinator crash and maintain telemetry throughput to observability (no >1% drop in reported events).
- Can reproduce two canonical scenarios: cold-KV burst and warmed-KV steady-state; p95 and tokens/sec for both are recorded and differ measurably.
- Per-tenant p95 gate implemented and validated in staging: a synthetic regression (inject 30% latency) triggers Alertmanager route within 6 minutes.
- Output formats: CSV and JSON summary per run with schema {tenant, protocol, scenario, tokens/sec, p50, p95, errors}.
- Integration tests: end-to-end smoke that runs SSE and WSS for a small load and asserts metrics presence in the observability index.

Testing matrix and scenarios:
- Protocols: SSE, WebSocket (secure and insecure), multiplexed per-connection counts: 1, 8, 32, 128.
- Cache states: cold (empty KV), warm (pre-warmed with representative prefix), partially-warm (20% prefixes hit).
- Traffic patterns: steady (poisson inter-arrival), bursty (Zipfian of session token bursts), connection churn (simulate 1–5% reconnections/min).
- Token sizes: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512 tokens), long (512–2048 tokens).

Observability and regression pipeline:
- Metrics sink: push metrics to Prometheus gateway; structured events to Loki.
- Baseline generation: run nightly baseline job that records per-tenant baselines for p95 and tokens/sec.
- Regression detection: service (small binary) subscribes to Prometheus TS and computes EWMA/log-drift per tenant; posts alerts to Alertmanager with runbook link.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Harness itself becomes a bottleneck for telemetry. Mitigation: batch telemetry and validate backpressure metrics; add sidecar to forward events directly from workers.
- Risk: synthetic prompts not representative. Mitigation: periodically refresh template corpus and run A/B comparisons vs anonymized production traces.
- Risk: alert noise. Mitigation: require sustained drift window + complimentary increase in error rate before page.

Runbook / How to run (dev/staging):
- k8s helm chart: values.yaml controls workers, multiplexing, tokens/sec target, scenario profile.
- Example dev command: helm --namespace perf-test upgrade --install harness ./charts/harness --set workers=10 --set multiplex=32 --set scenario=warm-steady --set targetTokensPerSec=50000 --set protocol=wss
- Post-run: upload run artifact to GCS and trigger dashboard refresh; run-summary uploader returns run URL.

Artifacts and links: 
- Prototype driver PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/421
- Baseline job config (confluence): https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Load+Baseline+Jobs
- Observability dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming-load-harness

Notes: This ticket focuses on the harness and regression gating; follow-up tickets will add automated rollout experiments to vary quantization/model-variant routing under load.
acceptance_criteria: Sustained 8h run with <1% telemetry drop and coordinator stable
Cold and warm KV scenarios produce distinct p95/tokens/sec profiles
Injected synthetic 30% latency regression triggers Alertmanager within 6 minutes
Run artifacts exported as CSV and JSON summaries with required schema
Smoke tests for SSE and WSS pass in CI with metrics verified in observability
